answer: In this PoA design, identity verification binds each claimed agent to a Wesolowski VDF: a seed undergoes continuous modular squaring in an RSA group of unknown order, while the output and proof certify the prescribed sequential work. Each squaring depends on its predecessor, so one identity’s computation cannot be parallelized across GPUs. Spawning clones therefore multiplies elapsed hardware time, and river, hollow, or relic labels provide no shortcut.
